clue.text: Zodiac sign contains 50 building blocks: they're to be read symbolically

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Aries the ram is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Lego is the toy brand of interlocking plastic building bricks

explanation.surface: An astrologer insists the star signs are packed with coded building blocks of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building blocks' is the toy brand, not a metaphor; 50 is a Roman numeral. Both go inside the star sign, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegories are stories whose characters and events stand for hidden moral or political ideas, so readers must interpret them symbolically.

clue.text: Cockney causes injury with weapons

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner's accent famously drops the breathy sound at the start of a word, so its opening letter goes

parts.note: to harm is to injure
the initial H is the letter a Cockney drops

explanation.surface: An East End tough hurts people using guns and knives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, famous for dropping the H sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms is the standard collective term for guns and other military weaponry, as in an arms dealer.

clue.text: I'd like to take part in ballet sometime

indicators.note: taking part of something means using only a portion of the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone wishes they could dance in a ballet one of these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is written without its apostrophe in the grid: the contraction of 'let us' that opens a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Let's' proposes doing something together, which expresses the same eager wish as saying you would like to do it.

clue.text: Suspect vague cliques with forgotten question: help me out here!

indicators.note: suspect material is unreliable and not as it seems, so the letters are rearranged
whatever is forgotten is left behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
Q is the standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by shadowy cliques, having lost track of the question, pleads for help.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the Q from the twelve letters first; the remaining eleven are rearranged. The phrase is also the title of a long-running BBC charades game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal pleas for a hint from someone who is stuck, the very request a puzzled solver makes.

clue.text: Some regrets in absorbing strong booze

indicators.note: 'some' means only a portion, so just part of the following letters is used

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: A drinker soaks up hard liquor along with a few regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts inside the first word and ends at the first letter of the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, a fairly loose example of booze.

clue.text: Australia missing 'reformed' parolees (they've run away)

indicators.note: to re-form is to shape again, so the letters are put into a new order
something missing is absent, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written
A is the international vehicle code for Austria, and here the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: Released prisoners in Australia have supposedly gone straight, though some have absconded.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'reformed' play on reformed criminals; it is really the signal to rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elopers are couples who run off secretly to marry, so the plural pronoun phrase describes them.

clue.text: Lying back, soaks in hot and steamy state

indicators.note: lying back means facing the other way, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to soak something is to wet it

explanation.surface: Someone reclines in a hot bath, soaking in a sauna-like haze.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 'state' of being in a stew; its 'hot and steamy' also suggests stew as cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being agitated and flustered, a worked-up emotional condition.

clue.text: HMRC device seeing dodge after unknown amount slipped into bill

indicators.note: slipping something into a thing places it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity
a dodge or a racket is a dishonest scheme

explanation.surface: The tax office spots a scam involving an undisclosed sum hidden in an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: HMRC is His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, the UK tax authority. The wordplay is read as RACKET placed after the bill with X slipped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax bracket is a band of income taxed at a set rate, a mechanism the revenue service uses to calculate liability.

clue.text: Feeble hope, year after year: getting clean

parts.note: a hope is a wish
Y is the abbreviation for year
to clean is to wash
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly hopes, year after year, to sober up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year after year' supplies both Ys: one Y follows each of the two other words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishy-washy describes something weak, insipid or lacking firmness, a close match for feeble.

clue.text: Drive time breaking Everyman in France; holiday about to be cancelled

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is inserted

parts.note: Everyman is the setter, so 'me'; in French that is moi
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: whatever is cancelled is struck out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday
ca. is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A road trip in France, with a long holiday abruptly called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calls himself Everyman, so he stands for 'me'. 'Drive' tempts as motoring, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Motivation is the inner urge or determination that pushes a person on, which is what drive means.

clue.text: No intro for jazz instruments (electric guitars)

indicators.note: with no introduction, the opening letter goes missing

parts.note: saxes are saxophones, staples of jazz

explanation.surface: A band leaves out the saxophone intro, letting the electric guitars take over.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets look like an aside, but they hold the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Axe is rock musicians' slang for a guitar, especially an electric one.

clue.text: Cartoon rodent drinking up brine mixed with a component of gin

indicators.note: to drink is to take something inside, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: Jerry is the mouse in the Tom and Jerry cartoons

indicators.note: mixed things are jumbled together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cartoon mouse gulps salty water laced with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of 'drinking up' but belongs to the letters that get rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin's dominant flavour comes from juniper berries, the essential botanical in every gin recipe.

clue.text: 50% of global occupations involving American household fittings

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up within, so one piece takes another inside
fifty per cent is half, so only half of the word's letters are kept

parts.note: the second half of the six-letter word
US is short for American
trades are occupations or jobs

explanation.surface: Half the world's jobs are said to involve fitting out American homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-word and the trades are joined first, and US is slipped in at the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Balustrades are railings with supporting posts along staircases and balconies, fixtures built into a house.

clue.text: Wistful odist, romanticizing daffodils, seen wandering o'er rises toward host, primarily!

definitions.text: Wistful odist, romanticizing daffodils, seen wandering o'er rises toward host, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.words: Wistful odist, romanticizing daffodils, seen wandering o'er rises toward host
parts.note: the initial letters of the ten words in turn

explanation.surface: A portrait of a dreamy poet who wanders hills and writes rapturously about a host of daffodils.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both spells the poet and describes him: 'I wandered lonely as a cloud' tells of seeing 'a host, of golden daffodils'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the Romantic poet whose best-known poem describes daffodils seen while wandering over the hills.

clue.text: With inward feet, slob takes long time to execute dance at first

parts.note: a slob is a pig, someone untidy and greedy
an eon is an immensely long period
taken as written

indicators.note: 'at first' points to the beginning, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy layabout with turned-in feet is slow to get going on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' applies to both of the last two words, taking one letter from each.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pigeon-toed walks with toes pointing inwards, so their feet turn in rather than straight.

clue.text: Bangkok: in a way, largely Asian city

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the city name ends in OK
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller's note that Bangkok is, in a way, a mostly Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final two letters of Bangkok are used, then 'in a way' with its last letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the capital-region city of the Japanese island prefecture of the same name, in East Asia.

clue.text: Country's spies turned, lust comes first

indicators.note: coming first means leading the line, so this piece is placed at the front
a turned wheel brings letters from the back round to the front

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A spy thriller in which agents defect because desire wins out over duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes first' places the turned word ahead of the spies. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: St Lucia is an independent island nation in the eastern Caribbean, a member of the Commonwealth.

clue.text: On the phone, one who sells rings; for engagement, he needs a second

definitions.text: for engagement, he needs a second

indicators.note: on the phone you only hear a word, never see how it is spelt

parts.note: a jeweller sells rings; in casual speech the two words can sound alike

explanation.surface: A ring seller phones about an engagement, saying he needs a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagement and second look like a marriage proposal and a moment's wait, but they mean a fight and the assistant in a formal duel.
explanation.definitionFit: In a formal duel each fighter is attended by a second, who arranges the encounter and stands by him.

clue.text: Search for intelligence … focus lacking, Everyman has to admit

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a recce is a military reconnaissance
the focus or centre of the five-letter word is its middle letter
the setter Everyman would say 'I've'

explanation.surface: A distracted setter confesses he must own up to his search for brains.
explanation.walkthrough: Recce is British military slang for reconnaissance. The setter refers to himself as Everyman, so he says 'I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in or accept them, as in receiving guests.

clue.text: Pray to tree, having taken hallucinogens

indicators.note: having taken something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: the beech is a common tree
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: A tripping hippy worships a tree after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so the plural Es stands for the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg earnestly, and pray has the same older sense of entreating someone.

clue.text: Conflict when Duke rejected redesigned wardrobe

indicators.note: a redesign changes the layout, so the letters are rearranged
something rejected is thrown out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Duke

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when a Duke turns down a remodelled wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a domestic squabble; the answer is a real war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer Wars were fought between Britain and the Boer republics of South Africa around 1900.

clue.text: Italian football team stuck in lavatory with German man. Unknown? This is perennial!

indicators.note: something stuck in a place is lodged inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: WC is water closet, a lavatory
Inter Milan is an Italian football club
Herr is the German for Mr
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A farcical tale of a whole Italian team trapped in a toilet with a German, who asks who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The team sits between the W and the C, and the German and unknown follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter cherry, also called Chinese lantern or physalis, is a plant that lives for many years, a perennial.

clue.text: Poster in which function's announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: sine is the trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A poster on which some event is advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party being publicised, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign and a poster are both displayed notices bearing written information for passers-by.

clue.text: Hi-tech Tokyo corporation on the rise for very long time

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means going up the grid, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: Sega is the Tokyo-based video games company

explanation.surface: A Japanese tech firm's shares have been climbing for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rise' sounds like business news but signals reading upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal plural meaning a long stretch, as in waiting for ages.

clue.text: In Oz, to get intimate with cricket captain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Australian slang for having sex
second meaning: Joe, who captained the England Test side

explanation.surface: An Australian wants to get close to the England skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is slang for Australia. Joe Root captained England's Test cricket team from 2017 to 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is vulgar Australian slang for intercourse and also the surname of a famous English batsman and captain.

clue.text: Did gin and went berserk for tenth anniversary

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple drank gin and lost control at their tenth-anniversary celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is fodder, not just part of 'went berserk'.
explanation.definitionFit: By tradition each wedding anniversary has a material, and tin marks ten years of marriage.

clue.text: Conceal whip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keep out of sight
second meaning: to flog or thrash

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is informal: to hide someone is to give them a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to keep something secret and, informally, to beat or thrash a person soundly.

clue.text: Stands for peers, stern, jumped-up

indicators.note: things jumped up are tossed in the air and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seats for the aristocracy, with a stern, self-important attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands' looks like seating and 'jumped-up' like an upstart, but these are the definition and the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for something is to symbolise or act on its behalf, which is what representing means.
